Pecan Pie

Served at: Thanksgiving Day (United States)

Serves 8Prep 20 minCook 50 min

Pecan Pie is a classic Southern dessert traditionally served during Thanksgiving Day in the United States. Its rich, sweet filling made with pecans and a buttery crust symbolizes the harvest and adds a festive touch to the holiday meal.

Ingredients

  • 1 unbaked 9-inch (23 cm) pie crust
  • 1 cup (200 g) light corn syrup
  • 1 cup (200 g) packed light brown sugar
  • 3 large eggs
  • 2 tablespoons (28 g) unsalted butter, melted
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 1 1/2 cups (180 g) pecan halves

Method

  1. Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
  2. Place the pie crust in a 9-inch pie pan and set aside.
  3. In a large bowl, whisk together the corn syrup, brown sugar, eggs, melted butter, vanilla extract, and salt until smooth.
  4. Stir in the pecan halves, ensuring they are evenly coated with the filling.
  5. Pour the pecan mixture into the prepared pie crust, spreading the pecans evenly.
  6. Bake for 50 minutes or until the filling is set and the crust is golden brown. If the crust edges brown too quickly, cover them with foil to prevent burning.
  7. Remove the pie from the oven and let it cool completely on a wire rack before serving.

Tips

  • Use a glass or metal pie dish for even baking.
  • For a richer flavor, toast the pecans lightly before adding to the filling.
  • Serve with whipped cream or vanilla ice cream for a classic presentation.
